# 10 · Styles, theming, motion

## CSS pipeline — `packages/flow/scripts/gen-styles.mjs`

Inputs: `src/styles/vendor/{init,base,style,node-resizer}.css` (copied by
`scripts/vendor-xyflow.sh`, never edited). Output (committed):

```
src/styles/generated/default.css.ts   init + style + node-resizer   (React's style.css)
src/styles/generated/base.css.ts      init + base + node-resizer    (React's base.css)
```

Steps per bundle: concatenate in that order → PostCSS with `postcss-nested` and
`postcss-rename({ strategy: (name) => name.replace(/^xy-flow/, 'lit-flow') })` → emit

```ts
// generated by scripts/gen-styles.mjs from xyflow@3d35b57 (MIT). Do not edit.
import { unsafeCSS } from 'lit';
export default unsafeCSS(`…css…`);
```

Escape backticks and `${` in the CSS text. CSS custom properties keep their `--xy-` names.
`.xyflow__viewport` doesn't appear in the CSS (it's only an engine hook), so the rename can't
touch it. Add a unit test that the output contains `.lit-flow__node` and no `.xy-flow`.

## Sheets — `styles/sheets.ts`

```ts
export const defaultSheets: CSSStyleSheet[];   // [default.css, extra.css]
export const baseSheets: CSSStyleSheet[];      // [base.css, extra.css]
export function adoptInto(root: Document | ShadowRoot, sheets: CSSStyleSheet[]): void; // append, dedupe by identity
```

Sheets are constructed once per page (`new CSSStyleSheet(); sheet.replaceSync(text)`) and
shared by every flow and plugin. `<xy-flow unstyled>` uses `baseSheets`; otherwise
`defaultSheets`. Plugins adopt the same array as their flow (they read it from the flow via
context; before the context arrives, `defaultSheets`).

## `extra.css.ts` (XY Lit additions)

Must include:

```css
.lit-flow__container { user-select: none; }
.lit-flow__edge-label { position: absolute; text-align: center; padding: 2px; font-size: 10px;
  color: var(--xy-edge-label-color, var(--xy-edge-label-color-default));
  background: var(--xy-edge-label-background-color, var(--xy-edge-label-background-color-default)); }
.lit-flow__edge-label.transparent { background: transparent; padding: 0; }
.lit-flow__selection { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; }
.lit-flow__node-toolbars { position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; z-index: 5; }
.lit-flow__node-toolbar { pointer-events: all; }
.lit-flow__a11y-hidden { display: none; }
.lit-flow__a11y-live { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; margin: -1px; border: 0; padding: 0;
  overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); clip-path: inset(100%); }
.lit-flow__loading { position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 10; display: grid; place-items: center;
  background: var(--xy-loading-background, var(--xy-background-color, var(--xy-background-color-default))); }
.lit-flow__loading[hidden] { display: none; }
.lit-flow__spinner { width: 28px; height: 28px; border-radius: 50%;
  border: 3px solid var(--xy-loading-track, rgba(0,0,0,.12)); border-top-color: var(--xy-loading-color, #555);
  animation: lit-flow-spin 0.8s linear infinite; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .lit-flow__spinner { animation-duration: 2.4s; } }
@keyframes lit-flow-spin { to { rotate: 360deg; } }
.lit-flow__node.remote-selected { outline: 2px solid var(--xy-remote-color); outline-offset: 2px; }
.lit-flow__node.remote-added { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--xy-remote-color); transition: box-shadow 1.2s ease-out; }
.lit-flow__node.remote-added.settled { box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 transparent; }
.lit-flow__node:not(:hover) > xy-node-resizer[variant='hover-corner'] .lit-flow__resize-control { opacity: 0; }
xy-node-resizer[variant='hover-corner'] .lit-flow__resize-control { transition: opacity 120ms; }
/* motion: see below */
```

The a11y description divs from `04` use the classes `lit-flow__a11y-hidden` and
`lit-flow__a11y-live`.

## Theming

- Every upstream `--xy-*` variable works; users set them on `xy-flow` (they inherit into the
  shadow root) or on `.lit-flow` via `::part`.
- `color-mode` sets class `light`/`dark` on `.lit-flow`; `system` follows `matchMedia`.
- `::part()` names: `pane`, `viewport`, `node`, `edge`, `edge-svg`, `handle`, `loading`,
  `panel` (in plugins), `background`, `button` (control buttons). Document that `::part` can't
  style descendants of a part, which is why `adoptStyles()` exists.
- `flow.adoptStyles(sheet)` for app stylesheets (e.g. a compiled Tailwind sheet). Node types'
  `styles` are adopted automatically.
- `render-root="light"`: no shadow root. Base sheets are adopted into the document (or the
  enclosing shadow root) once. Global CSS (Tailwind) then styles node content directly.

## Loading overlay

```html
<div class="lit-flow__loading" part="loading" ?hidden=${!showLoading}>
  <slot name="loading"><div class="lit-flow__spinner" role="status" aria-label="Loading diagram"></div></slot>
</div>
```

`showLoading = !noLoadingOverlay && (loading || !firstRenderComplete)`. `firstRenderComplete` is
set by `RenderCompleteController` and never reset, except when a new `source` is attached
(collab rooms switching).

## Motion — `motion.ts`

```ts
type MotionState = {
  mode: 'off' | 'enter' | 'enter remote';
  enabled: boolean;                  // mode !== 'off' && !reducedMotion && visibleNodeCount <= motionMaxNodes
  entering: ReadonlySet<string>;     // node ids that should animate in now
  enteringEdges: ReadonlySet<string>;
};
```

The store computes `entering` in `setNodesFromSource`: new ids in the **initial population**
(first non-empty node set after mount or `setSource`) always qualify when enabled; new ids in
later updates qualify only when `mode === 'enter remote'` and `source.lastUpdateRemote` is true.
Stagger index = order among entering nodes.

Node entrance (`<xy-node>`): when its id is in `entering` and it first becomes measured, add
class `entering` and style `--xy-enter-index: i`; remove the class on `animationend` (or after
`duration + stagger·i + 100 ms` as a backstop).

```css
.lit-flow__node.entering { animation: lit-flow-enter var(--xy-enter-duration, 260ms) var(--xy-enter-easing, cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)) both;
  animation-delay: calc(var(--xy-enter-index, 0) * var(--xy-enter-stagger, 18ms)); }
@keyframes lit-flow-enter { from { opacity: 0; scale: 0.96; translate: 0 6px; } to { opacity: 1; scale: 1; translate: 0 0; } }
.lit-flow__edge.entering .lit-flow__edge-path { animation: lit-flow-draw var(--xy-enter-duration, 260ms) ease-out both;
  animation-delay: calc(var(--xy-enter-index, 0) * var(--xy-enter-stagger, 18ms) + 120ms); }
@keyframes lit-flow-draw { to { stroke-dashoffset: 0; } }
```

`scale`/`translate` are individual transform properties, so they compose with the inline
`transform: translate(x, y)` that positions the node.

Edge draw-in (`<xy-edge>`): when the edge id is in `enteringEdges` (edges whose both endpoints
are entering), after first render read `path.getTotalLength()` and set inline
`stroke-dasharray: L; stroke-dashoffset: L` on the edge path plus class `entering`; on
`animationend` or the backstop timeout remove the inline styles and the class (restores any
user dash style, e.g. animated edges).

Remote highlights: when `mode === 'enter remote'` and an entering node has
`node.remote?.addedBy`, `<xy-node>` sets `--xy-remote-color` to that user's colour and class
`remote-added`, then adds `settled` after one frame so the box-shadow fades out.
Independently of motion, `<xy-node>` maps `node.remote.selectedBy[0]` to class
`remote-selected` + `--xy-remote-color`, and `draggingBy`/`resizingBy` to class
`remote-dragging` (CSS: `transition: transform 80ms linear`, smoothing ~30–60 Hz awareness
updates; keep the class for 150 ms after the drag ends so the committed position eases in).

## Wheel-scroll detection — `wheel.ts`

Attached by `<xy-flow>` to its `.lit-flow__nodes` container (a descendant of the XYPanZoom
element, so it runs before d3-zoom's listener) as a passive `wheel` listener, unless
`wheel-scroll-detection="off"`:

```ts
function onWheel(e: WheelEvent) {
  if (e.ctrlKey) return;                                   // pinch-zoom gesture: let XYPanZoom handle it
  for (const el of e.composedPath()) {
    if (!(el instanceof HTMLElement)) continue;
    if (el.classList.contains('lit-flow__node')) break;    // stop at the node boundary
    if (canScroll(el, e.deltaX, e.deltaY)) { e.stopPropagation(); return; }
  }
}
function canScroll(el: HTMLElement, dx: number, dy: number): boolean {
  const s = getComputedStyle(el);
  const y = /(auto|scroll|overlay)/.test(s.overflowY) && el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight &&
    ((dy < 0 && el.scrollTop > 0) || (dy > 0 && el.scrollTop + el.clientHeight < el.scrollHeight - 1));
  const x = /(auto|scroll|overlay)/.test(s.overflowX) && el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth &&
    ((dx < 0 && el.scrollLeft > 0) || (dx > 0 && el.scrollLeft + el.clientWidth < el.scrollWidth - 1));
  return y || x;
}
```

`stopPropagation` keeps the event from reaching d3-zoom, so the browser scrolls the element
natively. Once it hits its limit, `canScroll` is false and the wheel pans or zooms the canvas
again. The `nowheel` class still works as upstream (XYPanZoom's own filter).

## Tests

- `styles.test.ts` (Node): generated CSS renamed correctly.
- `motion.browser.test.ts`: entering classes only on initial population, honours reduced
  motion (emulate with `matchMedia` stub) and `motion-max-nodes`; inline dash removed after the
  animation.
- `wheel.browser.test.ts`: wheel over a scrollable node scrolls it and leaves the viewport
  unchanged until the end; `off` restores panning; `ctrlKey` wheel still zooms.
